title: adaptive-connection-shedding-and-transparent-retry-attenuator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During multiple customer escalations over the past two weeks we observed coordinated tenant retry storms that amplified transient backend latency into widespread 5xx and timeout waves. This ticket implements an "adaptive connection shedding" mechanism at the edge proxy and introduces a transparent retry attenuator layer to prevent amplification while preserving good tenants' success rates. The change is intended to be a low-risk runtime shim with a controlled canary rollout and explicit diagnostics for post-incident analysis.
context: Symptoms: sudden spikes in 5xx and client-visible timeouts correlated with tenant burst events. Root cause (partial): retries from SDKs and client libraries combined with queueing at the frontdoor proxy and slow KV cache evictions. Existing circuit-breaker thresholds are too coarse and do not account for queued-in-flight request amplification. Related incidents: multiple customer escalations and PagerDuty bridges in Feb 2025.
progress_updates: 2025-02-10: Triage call with SRE, runtime, and API teams. Short-term mitigation: increase proxy admission timeout to avoid immediate client-facing 5xx while we instrument queues.
2025-02-12: Prototype of connection-shedding logic completed. Proof-of-concept exposes per-tenant queued-count metric and reclassement priority window.

2025-02-14: Integrated transparent retry attenuator in SDK proxy layer (server-side) to rewrite aggressive client retries into backoff-aware retries. Added heuristics to keep idempotent calls unaffected.
2025-02-16: End-to-end tests and loadbench run in staging simulating tenant burst patterns (10x normal). Observed 60% reduction in distributed 5xx propagation compared to baseline.
2025-02-18: Preparing canary rollout with gradated admission limits and feature flag. Documented rollback triggers (in metrics) and runbook additions for on-call.
decision: Ship a two-part change: 1) Edge proxy: per-tenant queue-length detection + adaptive shedding (configurable hysteresis + minimum grace windows). 2) Transparent retry attenuator: a middleware that intercepts aggressive retries and converts them to server-coordinated backoff tokens to avoid duplicate work. Both behind feature flags and initially enabled only for a 5% traffic canary for impacted regions.
acceptance_criteria: Canary sustains 72h with no customer-visible SLA regressions for critical tenants
End-to-end dashboards show >=50% reduction in cross-tenant 5xx spread during synthetic burst tests
No uptick in latency for pinned low-latency tenants beyond 5th percentile baseline
Rollout and rollback documented in oncall runbook and validated by SRE tabletop exercise
rollback_plan: Feature flags can be toggled per-region and per-tenant. Rollback triggers: sustained increase in error-rate for high-priority tenants, unexpected client failures traced to attenuator heuristics, or CPU/latency regressions >20% over baseline. On rollback, immediately revert proxy admission changes and disable attenuator; inform customers via status page and open a postmortem channel.
notes_for_support: Include guidance for Support: If a customer reports increased 5xx after canary, capture full request IDs and tenant id, note whether SDK is in-use, and toggle 'attenuator' flag for that tenant as a temporary mitigation. Use the 'queued_count' and 'retry_token_drop' metrics when filing follow-ups.
post_deploy_tasks: Monitor per-tenant queued_count, retry_token_drop, and error-spread metrics for first 7 days
Run a cross-functional retro with PM, SRE, Runtime, and Support at end of canary
If stable, schedule rollout to 25% and then 100% with 48h observation windows
